best_for: Desktop PC builders on Windows 10 or 11 who want case, CPU and GPU fans on curves tied to the right sensors, instead of juggling each board maker's utility.
description:
FanControl is a fan speed app for Windows made by Rémi Mercier, a developer who also keeps its documentation on getfancontrol.com. A guided setup takes you through the first launch, and you can change the theme and colors of the window to suit your taste.

Once it runs, you can keep several profiles, say a quiet one for the night and a loud one for gaming, and switch between them. Response time, hysteresis and step up and step down settings stop fans from revving at every short spike. Avoid points keep a fan away from a speed where it rattles. Temperatures can sit in the tray as icons, and the app can start at boot as a service, before anyone signs in. Plugins, dropped in as a DLL file, add sensors from other hardware.

points.title: One app for every fan
points.text: It reads sensors through LibreHardwareMonitor and drives motherboard, GPU and some AIO fans from one window. Each fan can follow its own curve, built from the temperature that matters to it.

points.title: Curves beyond a simple graph
points.text: You get linear, graph, flat, trigger, sync and auto curves, plus mix curves that take the max, min, average or sum of several. Calibration maps each fan's start, stop and top speed, so a curve can aim at an RPM instead of a percentage.

points.title: Laptops mostly will not work
points.text: The README says laptops do not expose their fans like desktop boards do. It may install and then find no fans at all, unless a plugin covers your model.

points.title: GPU fans have floors
points.text: On recent NVIDIA cards manual control bottoms out at 30 percent. On AMD cards, applying a fan setting resets Adrenaline overclock settings to defaults.

points.title: Free, but closed source
points.text: The app is free with optional donations. The source is closed; the GitHub repository holds releases and the issue tracker.

points.title: Update past V237
points.text: Builds up to V237 shipped the old WinRing0 driver, which Windows Defender flags and which leaves sensors undetected. V238 and later use PawnIO instead. The README adds that the app, installer and updater are now signed. This site keeps 97 Windows versions, with an installer and a portable ZIP for x64.
